tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

schema.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

name: email-segments-skip-recently-emailed
description: "JusPrin 2 SendGrid segments exclude earlier batches with the jusprin2_sent=t contact field (tag each batch after it's sent); never OR \"Last Emailed\" beside other rules"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: c2adecd8-a1fc-4e82-9512-79ed47bbae43
  modified: 2026-11-14T18:07:58.929Z
---

Kenneth wants every later JusPrin 2 email segment (SendGrid legacy Marketing Campaigns) to leave out anyone an earlier JusPrin 2 batch already reached. On 2026-11-13 he chose a contact marker for this. He passed the request on through another session.

**Why:** so no one gets the launch email twice.

**How to apply:**
- Each contact has a text custom field, `jusprin2_sent`, created 2026-11-13. On that day it was set to `t` for all 514 people in batch 1 (campaign 22621835, 310 people) and batch 2 (campaign 22624323, 204 people), using a CSV upload with the columns `email,jusprin2_sent` and the "Add contacts" option (no list). The upload updated existing contacts and added none: All Contacts stayed at 48,401.
- Every new segment gets one more AND rule: `jusprin2_sent is not t`. Verified: on All Contacts it counts 47,887, which is 48,401 minus 514, so contacts with no value in the field stay in.
- After each new batch is sent (not before), upload its recipients the same way with `jusprin2_sent=t`.
- Never pair "Last Emailed is empty" OR "Last Emailed is before <date>" with other rules. The editor can't group rules, and the OR let in extra people: batch 2's segment went from 204 to 796. The marker covers only JusPrin 2 batches, not other recent emails.
- Before pointing a campaign at a segment, compare its count with a count of your own, for example from the contacts export.
- Batch 3 (built 2026-11-14, a subject x sender-name test): 2,414 contacts carry `jusprin2_arm` = b3a..b3d; segments 14025814-17, draft campaigns 22625856-59. Tag them `jusprin2_sent=t` after they're sent, and read results per `jusprin2_arm` group.
- Test segment "TEST ONLY - jusprin2_sent check 2026-11-13" (14023795, currently `is not t`) is left in SendGrid. Delete it only when Kenneth says.

metadata:

On 2026-11-14 Kenneth decided the big (~300k contacts) marketing send stays on SendGrid legacy Marketing Campaigns. Brevo was set up first (obico.io authenticated, em.obico.io link branding, senders verified, phone verified; free plan, nothing bought) and was then dropped.

**Why:** Brevo suspends the account when a campaign to newly imported contacts has unsubscribes above 1%, hard bounces above 2% or complaints above 0.2% (help article 360017299259), and a second suspension is permanent. SendGrid history across 295 campaigns: every large send since 2024 had 1.6-3.3% unsubscribes (2.9% for 2025, 2.5% for 2026), bounces 0.2-6.8%, spam reports 0.00-0.05%. Only the recent JusPrin 2 batches (recent JusPrin users) stayed near 1%.

**How to apply:** Don't propose moving the bulk list to Brevo (or any provider with similar first-send suspension rules) without first addressing the unsubscribe rate. The Brevo account and its six obico.io DNS records (brevo-code TXT, brevo1/brevo2._domainkey, em, r.em, img.em CNAMEs) were left in place; remove them only if Kenneth asks. Related: [[email-segments-skip-recently-emailed]].

# Read-only. Contacts for the SendGrid TSD list: every JusPrin 1 user, plus every Obico user active in the
# last 360 days (the activeusers.csv rule in tsd-enterprise/scripts/export_for_sendgrid.sql).
# opted_in and dormant_pro follow that script's definitions.
import csv, io
from datetime import timedelta
from django.conf import settings
from django.db.models import Max
from django.utils import timezone
from app.models import User, Syndicate
from app.jusprin.models import JusPrinChat
from app.accounts import users_by_email
from jusprin.models import JusPrinPlan
from app_ent.models import Subscription

now = timezone.now()
last = dict(JusPrinChat.objects.filter(user__syndicate__name='base').values('user_id').annotate(m=Max('created_at')).values_list('user_id', 'm'))
paying = {p.user_id for p in JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(plan_id__in=settings.JUSPRIN_V1_PLANS, user__syndicate__name='base') if p.is_active}
jv2 = Syndicate.objects.get(name='jusprinv2')
pro_ids = set(Subscription.objects.exclude(plan_id='pro-trial').filter(expired_at__isnull=True).values_list('user_id', flat=True))
d = lambda t: t.strftime('%m/%d/%Y') if t else ''
users = User.objects.filter(syndicate__name='base', is_active=True).exclude(email='').filter(
    models_q := __import__('django.db.models', fromlist=['Q']).Q(id__in=last.keys()) | __import__('django.db.models', fromlist=['Q']).Q(last_active_at__gt=now - timedelta(days=360)))
out = io.StringIO(); w = csv.writer(out)
w.writerow(['email', 'first_name', 'last_name', 'opted_in', 'date_joined', 'last_active_at', 'dormant_pro',
            'is_jusprin_user', 'jusprin1_last_chat', 'jusprin1_paid', 'jusprin2_user'])
n = 0
for u in users.iterator():
    dormant = u.id in pro_ids and (u.last_active_at is None or u.last_active_at < now - timedelta(days=30))
    row = [u.email, u.first_name or '', u.last_name or '', 't' if u.account_notification_by_email else 'f',
           d(u.date_joined), d(u.last_active_at), 't' if dormant else 'f']
    if u.id in last:
        row += ['t', d(last[u.id]), 't' if u.id in paying else 'f', 't' if list(users_by_email(u.email.lower(), jv2)) else 'f']
    else:
        row += ['', '', '', '']
    w.writerow(row); n += 1
print('CSVSTART'); print(out.getvalue(), end=''); print('CSVEND', n)

Deleting contacts in SendGrid doesn't clear unsubscribes. Suppression lists are stored separately from contacts, so the unsubscribe records usually stay in place.

- **Contacts and suppressions are separate.** SendGrid's documentation says contact storage isn't linked to suppression lists, and changing or deleting contacts under Marketing > Contacts doesn't remove addresses from the Suppressions tab. Suppression lists are repositories of addresses that will have requests dropped, and they do not count toward contact storage. Dropped requests can still use email credits.
- **Removing a suppression is a separate step.** SendGrid's guide for removing a single contact from an unsubscribe list says to search by email address and select only that contact. It also warns to check the Group Name so you remove the address from the correct unsubscribe group. Please pay attention to the Group Name for your selected contact to ensure you delete this from the correct Unsubscribe Group.
- **Legacy API endpoints exist, but they're deprecated.** The legacy Marketing Campaigns API includes endpoints to delete a recipient and to delete a list. The docs label these as the obsolete Legacy Marketing Campaigns API. SendGrid points users to the newer Marketing Campaigns APIs for current guidance.
- **Deleting an unsubscribe group has side effects.** Per the suppression group API docs, if a recipient uses the "one-click unsubscribe" option on an email associated with a deleted group, that recipient will be added to the global suppression list.

Caveat: these results come from SendGrid's current support and API docs, not from a source that addresses the legacy-campaign deletion case directly. The support pages also suggest the legacy and new Marketing Campaigns UIs differ, so check the steps against your account's interface.

Kenneth wants every later JusPrin 2 email segment (SendGrid legacy Marketing Campaigns) to leave out anyone an earlier JusPrin 2 batch already reached. On 2026-11-13 he chose a contact marker for this. He passed the request on through another session.

**Why:** so no one gets the launch email twice.

**How to apply:**
- Each contact has a text custom field, `jusprin2_sent`, created 2026-11-13. On that day it was set to `t` for all 514 people in batch 1 (campaign 22621835, 310 people) and batch 2 (campaign 22624323, 204 people), using a CSV upload with the columns `email,jusprin2_sent` and the "Add contacts" option (no list). - Batch 3 (built 2026-11-14, a subject x sender-name test): 2,414 contacts carry `jusprin2_arm` = b3a..b3d; segments 14025814-17, draft campaigns 22625856-59. Tag them `jusprin2_sent=t` after they're sent, and read results per `jusprin2_arm` group.

content.text:
Everything is ready for SendGrid to hold only the current batch. One thing is left before deleting the 48,401 contacts: your yes. Nothing has been deleted.

**What I saved.** The folder `/Users/kenneth/.claude/jusprin2-email-data/` is readable only by you and is in no git repository. It holds:
- the 514 people batches 1 and 2 went to;
- the 2,414 people picked for batch 3, kept in a separate file because they haven't been sent yet;
- the 37,798 contacts we built from the Obico database and uploaded on Nov 12, with the query that built them;
- a README explaining how to keep the record up to date.

**Who opened and clicked.** SendGrid stores this on each contact, so deleting the contacts would lose it. Before that happens, I copied it for batches 1 and 2 into the same folder. Batch 1 had 53 people open and 1 click. Batch 2 had 51 open and 2 click. Those are the same numbers SendGrid's campaign stats show.

**Unsubscribes survive deleting the contact.** Both campaigns put unsubscribes into one SendGrid unsubscribe group, called "The Spaghetti Detective". That group is a separate list from the contacts. I took the first 43 people on it, unsubscribed between 2019 and 2026. 39 of them are no longer stored as contacts, and they are still on the list. SendGrid's docs say the same: deleting contacts doesn't remove anyone from the suppression lists ([SendGrid support](https://support.sendgrid.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408817749019)). I didn't delete a test contact to prove it directly, because that would be a deletion you hadn't approved, and the evidence above seemed enough.

**Decision needed: what to delete, and when.** Deleting every contact also deletes batch 3. Those 2,414 people are already sorted into the four subject-and-sender test groups. Four draft campaigns point at them, and the other session is still waiting for your go on those drafts. There are two ways to do it:
- **Keep batch 3.** Delete the other 45,987 contacts and keep batch 3 until it's sent and its results are in, then delete it too. If batch 3 is still stored in December, December's bill is about $10, because 2,414 is just over the 2,000 free contacts.
- **Delete everything.** Batch 3 would have to be uploaded again and its four groups and drafts rebuilt.

Deleting any time before December 1 saves the same amount, since November's bill is already set. My pick is to keep batch 3.

**One gap before deleting.** The folder doesn't have a copy of about 10,600 of the 48,401 contacts. They were in SendGrid before our Nov 12 upload, and they exist only there. If future batches come from the Obico database, you don't need them. If you want a copy anyway, SendGrid's "Export CSV" button downloads one, and I'll ask before downloading it.

**After this, each batch works like this:**
1. Build the batch from the database.
2. Drop everyone in the sent record and everyone on the unsubscribe lists.
3. Upload and send.
4. Copy the opens and clicks a day or two later.
5. Add the batch to the sent record and delete it from SendGrid.

python3 - <<EOF
import hashlib,csv
S='$S';D='$D'
raw=''.join(open(f'{S}/b3c{i}').read().rstrip('\n') for i in range(1,8))
print('len',len(raw))
arms={}
for r in csv.DictReader(open(D+'/batch3_arms_NOT_YET_SENT.csv')):
    e=r[[k for k in r if 'mail' in k][0]].strip().lower(); arms[e]=r['jusprin2_arm']
hm={}
for e in arms: hm.setdefault(hashlib.sha256(e.encode()).hexdigest()[:8],[]).append(e)
print('emails',len(arms),'hash collisions',sum(len(v)>1 for v in hm.values()))
rows=[];cur=None;miss=0
for t in raw.split():
    if t.startswith('#'): cid,ev=t[1:].split('_'); continue
    if t not in hm: miss+=1; continue
    rows.append((cid,ev,hm[t][0],arms[hm[t][0]]))
from collections import Counter
print(Counter((c,e) for c,e,_,_ in rows),'unmatched',miss)
with open(D+'/batch3_opens_clicks_2026-11-16.csv','w') as f:
    f.write('campaign_id,event,email,jusprin2_arm\n'); f.writelines(','.join(r)+'\n' for r in rows)
EOF

Kenneth wants every later JusPrin 2 email segment (SendGrid legacy Marketing Campaigns) to leave out anyone an earlier JusPrin 2 batch already reached. On 2026-11-13 he chose a contact marker for this. He passed the request on through another session.

**Why:** so no one gets the launch email twice.

**How to apply:**
- Each contact has a text custom field, `jusprin2_sent`, created 2026-11-13. On that day it was set to `t` for all 514 people in batch 1 (campaign 22621835, 310 people) and batch 2 (campaign 22624323, 204 people), using a CSV upload with the columns `email,jusprin2_sent` and the "Add contacts" option (no list). Pass before_uuid="c_e0922caaf868ede020b0ad9d" to page further back.

[assistant] So far the download button hasn't helped. Version A of batch 4 ended with a plain "Download JusPrin 2:" line and the GitHub address. Version B had a purple "Download JusPrin 2" button in its place. About 27 hours in, version A has slightly more clicks on every link, though only one of the gaps is bigger than chance would explain.

| | A: plain link | B: button | Could be chance? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delivered | 1,691 | 1,665 | |
| Opened | 28.1% | 29.4% | yes (p = 0.44) |
| Clicked anything | 3.3% | 2.7% | yes (p = 0.30) |
| Clicked download | 27 (1.6%) | 18 (1.1%) | yes (p = 0.19) |
| Clicked the video | 50 | 39 | yes (p = 0.27) |
| Clicked the announcement | 19 (1.1%) | 6 (0.4%) | no (p = 0.01) |
| Unsubscribed | 1.8% | 1.1% | yes (p = 0.13) |
| Bounced | 1.4% | 3.0% | no (p = 0.002) |

The link counts are total clicks, so someone who clicked twice counts twice. That's the only per-link number SendGrid gives.

**What this suggests so far**
- **The button didn't raise downloads.** If anything it went the other way, but the gap is small enough to be chance.
- **The announcement lost clicks in the button version.** In version A it was a bare URL on its own line. In version B it was the short words "Read the announcement" in the sentence after the button. My guess is that the short inline link is easy to miss. That's a guess, not something this test measured.
- **The button version bounced twice as often: 52 against 25.** The two groups were split at random, so a gap this large is odd. One possible cause is that some mail servers reject the button's HTML. I haven't checked yet. Tomorrow I'll look at the bounce reasons for each version.

**The missed check**
The 11:49 job vanished without running even though the Mac was awake and the app was running. Tomorrow's 48-hour read at 11:53 AM uses the same kind of job, so it could be lost the same way. If you don't see a report from me by about noon, a one-line nudge will start it. That read saves batch 4's opens and clicks permanently and tells the rollout session it can delete the SendGrid contacts. SendGrid will also need to still be signed in.

I added these numbers to the shared note, `jusprin2-batch1-low-opens.md`.

import hashlib,csv
from collections import Counter
S='$S';D='/Users/kenneth/.claude/jusprin2-email-data'
raw=open(S+'/b4raw').read().rstrip('\n').replace('[javascript_tool:javascript_exec]','')
print('len',len(raw))
arms={r['email'].strip().lower():r['jusprin2_arm'] for r in csv.DictReader(open(D+'/batch4_arms_sent_2026-11-16.csv'))}
hm={}
for e in arms: hm.setdefault(hashlib.sha256(e.encode()).hexdigest()[:8],[]).append(e)
print('emails',len(arms),'collisions',sum(len(v)>1 for v in hm.values()))
rows=[];miss=[]
for t in raw.split():
    if t.startswith('#'): cid,ev=t[1:].split('_'); continue
    if t not in hm: miss.append(t); continue
    rows.append((cid,ev,hm[t][0],arms[hm[t][0]]))
print(Counter((c,e,a) for c,e,_,a in rows),'unmatched',miss)
with open(D+'/batch4_opens_clicks_2026-11-17.csv','w') as f:
    f.write('campaign_id,event,email,jusprin2_arm\n'); f.writelines(','.join(r)+'\n' for r in rows)

content.text:
Yes, and it's done: all 48,401 contacts are deleted, and SendGrid's All Contacts now shows 0. The next batch can be uploaded on its own.

**What I saved before deleting.** Batch 4 went out yesterday and was already in the permanent list of people emailed. The only thing missing was who opened and clicked it. SendGrid keeps that on each contact, so I saved it first, about 27 hours after the send. The counts matched SendGrid:

| | Opened | Clicked |
|---|---|---|
| Version A: plain download link | 478 | 56 |
| Version B: download button | 492 | 46 |

I also saved the daily totals for every JusPrin 2 campaign as a backup. Both files are in `/Users/kenneth/.claude/jusprin2-email-data/`.

**What survived the delete.** I checked two things afterwards:
- Each campaign's totals: opens, clicks and bounces still show in SendGrid.
- The unsubscribe list: still there, so people who unsubscribed stay blocked.

**What's gone from SendGrid.** These now exist only in the email-data folder:
- the contacts themselves;
- the markers that said who was already emailed and which test group each person was in;
- per-person opens and clicks.

**Tomorrow's 48-hour batch 4 check.** The [session running it](#local_e52b8140-361c-40af-bede-d69b144a2911) can still read campaign totals, clicks per link and bounce reasons. It can no longer see which individual people opened or clicked after today. I've told it, and told it not to overwrite the file I saved.

**For each batch from now on:**
1. Build the batch from the database.
2. Leave out everyone in `jusprin2_sent_all.csv` and everyone on the unsubscribe list.
3. Upload only that batch and send it.
4. Save its opens and clicks.
5. Delete it from SendGrid.

As long as each batch stays under 2,000 people, SendGrid charges nothing for storing them.

content.text:
Yes, as far as the batch filter allows. Every JusPrin 1 user it lets through has been emailed: 6,546 people across the four batches. These counts come from the Nov 12 snapshot of the database. Anyone who started using JusPrin 1 after Nov 12 isn't counted, which should be very few people.

**The 238 JusPrin 1 users who weren't emailed:**
- **191 turned off email from us.** They should never get this email.
- **24 are paying Obico Pro subscribers who haven't been active for 30 days or more.** The filter used to build every batch left this group out. I couldn't find where that rule came from or who set it.
- **20 still pay for JusPrin 1.** The [session planning the move to JusPrin 2](#local_87a60f59-f953-4ea7-b0fb-1f96b66823b6) handles them separately: you move each one by hand in Chargebee once they've signed up for JusPrin 2.
- **2 already have a JusPrin 2 account.**
- **1 I can't explain.** It passes the filter but wasn't in any batch.

**Decision needed: who gets the next batch.** The next group is Obico users who never used JusPrin. There are 28,913 of them who were active in the last year and haven't opted out:

| Last active | People |
|---|---|
| Within 30 days | 11,265 |
| 30 to 90 days ago | 4,159 |
| 90 to 180 days ago | 4,515 |
| 180 to 360 days ago | 8,974 |

There are two catches:
- **The email has to be different.** All four batches so far said "JusPrin 2 is here" to people who already knew JusPrin. Obico users mostly don't, so they need an email that introduces JusPrin itself.
- **These are Obico customers.** Some pay for Obico, and an email they don't want could cost us subscribers. For JusPrin 1 users, 1 to 2% unsubscribed per batch; SendGrid's records show 1.6 to 3.3% for past large sends to Obico users.

My pick is Obico users active within the last 30 days, the most recently active first. Send in batches of up to 2,000 so SendGrid storage stays free. For subject and sender, use what won in batch 3: the new subject, from "Kenneth from JusPrin", which got 32% opens against 25 to 29% for the other three versions. Before the first batch goes out, the new email needs writing and your approval.

The other way is to email the 24 dormant Obico Pro subscribers first. That only makes sense if no one deliberately decided to leave them out.

- **Title, chosen 2026-11-02 late evening ("ok go with a"):** "The AI slicer that fixes failed prints." Kenneth's brief: the title must be short and say what JusPrin is for, and it must say AI; the earlier "Your print failed. Ask someone who can see why." lost because it named neither the slicer nor the AI. Subtitle for patient readers: "Show it a photo of what went wrong. The agent reads your file, your settings and your slice, changes the settings and slices again." The line "Pick how the agent should think. Decided 2026-11-02 (late), in the session that critiqued the onboarding wizard against the pricing goals.

Kenneth: "I feel more strongly about expert help too." "Simpler slicing" was the other candidate; it is what keeps people, not what brings them.
- **First launch:** one welcome screen, no wizard, split: the clip on the left, the headline and doors on the right.
- **Title, chosen 2026-11-02 late evening ("ok go with a"):** "The AI slicer that fixes failed prints." Kenneth's brief: the title must be short and say what JusPrin is for, and it must say AI; the earlier "Your print failed. Ask someone who can see why." lost because it named neither the slicer nor the AI. Subtitle for patient readers: "Show it a photo of what went wrong. The agent reads your file, your settings and your slice, changes the settings and slices again." The line "Pick how the agent should think. Change it any time in Preferences › Agent." sits as a label directly above the doors. The runner-up was F, "Slice with AI. Fix failed prints tonight.", the only one carrying the no-waiting comparison.
- **Doors, Kenneth's pick "One primary":** the first-month offer card with "Sign in for 500 credits" on top, then two equal slim rows, "Your own API key · Free" and "Claude Code or Claude Desktop · Free · MCP server", then "Just slice for now" as a link. Every free door shows its cost; nothing is hidden. Kenneth's worry was feeling pushed to the cloud; the answer is honest cost lines and the reversibility line, not equal pixel size.
- **The clip:** about 12 s (Kenneth cut it from 25: "nobody has the patience to wait for it to finish"), silent, looping. Four beats, one caption each: "Show it what happened." / "It reads your photo, your file and your slice." / "It changes the settings for you." / "And slices again. Tonight." Motion only at beat changes, short holds, last frame longest. The failed print is a real CC BY 2.0 photo of a stringing blue-and-white 3DBenchy (Flickr 19273965123, #3DBenchy account; chosen over a peeled black hull because the strings are failure and cause in one picture); beat 1 shows the intact boat on the plate beside it; beat 3 shows two big settings, Retraction 0.8 → 2 mm and Nozzle 220 → 200 °C; beat 4 is a bar labelled "Slicing NN%" that, at 100 %, fades the stringy thumbnail to a clean print of the same boat (Flickr 19239738473, CC BY 2.0), then a green check and "Sliced · ready · 1 h 34 min · 34 g". No confetti, no time-lapse. The agent's words and the setting values are placeholders until a live run is recorded for this photo; the shipped clip is a recording of the real app. CC BY needs a visible credit in the app; the first-run branch puts it in a "Photo credits" disclosure under the clip.
- **Logo, header, footer (2026-11-02, late):** the welcome is a full-window screen with no shell header (the breadcrumb and "Agent not connected" status read as an error before a choice) and no footer sentence. The brand lockup sits top-left of the window as a corner anchor, 43 px tall (120 px wide, the design-system minimum), the way Stripe, Dropbox, Zoom, Canva and Figma anchor theirs on split sign-in screens; Kenneth called a lockup or lone mark placed inside the content column above the title "pretty ugly" and asked to "check how other products do that" rather than reinvent. Nine captured first screens of those products showed a centred small mark above the title, or a wordmark top-left of the window; never a display-size lockup in the content column.
- **After the welcome:** an OrcaSlicer import belongs on a conditional screen right after the door, asked (not silent like the v1 import in `V1Import/`), shown only when an OrcaSlicer folder exists; the same action lives later in Home's Printers column and the add-printer form. Follow-up screens per door: sign-in in the browser then Home with the agent connected; own key and MCP open Preferences › Agent; Just slice goes to Home with the doors collapsed in the agent column. Not yet drawn: Home after Just slice, the assumed-printer chip.
- **Wall of text:** under about 30 words outside the clip. The transcript panel that duplicated the clip was the failure.
- **Method:** Kenneth stopped the design session ("a lot more effective if we explore this way"): render a few 1280×800 screens from the app's tokens with headless Chrome, send PNGs, iterate.

**Why:** the wizard asked for commitment before showing value; the proposition decides the headline, the proof and the door order, so it had to be settled first.

**How to apply:** the canvas boards from [[first-run-flow-boards]] (variants A and B) predate these decisions; variant B's welcome is the nearer one but its headline, weighting and proof must follow this note. Say "AI" to a first-time visitor and introduce "the agent" in the subtitle; keep "Agent" explained, never "trial", no dollar figure on the offer. Related: [[sign-up-reason-must-be-prominent]], [[show-the-board-when-asking-kenneth]], [[mockup-strings-from-real-output]].

content.text:
The test group is built and both emails are drafted below. Nothing has been uploaded to SendGrid or sent.

**Who gets it.** Production has 4,110 Obico users who were last active 30 to 90 days ago. None of them ever used JusPrin 1, has a JusPrin 2 account, has opted out of email, or has been emailed before. I left out 295 paying Obico Pro subscribers who haven't been active for 30 days or more, the same filter as every earlier batch.

I split the list at random:
- 1,000 people get version A.
- 1,000 people get version B.
- 2,110 are held back for whichever version wins.

The two groups match in mix, for example about 70% Gmail in each. Storing these contacts in SendGrid costs nothing extra this month, because November's bill is already set. I'll delete them before December 1.

**The two versions.**
- **A: what won before.** Subject "JusPrin 2 is here", from "Kenneth from JusPrin" <support@obico.io>.
- **B: introduces JusPrin to Obico users.** Subject "From Obico: an AI slicer that fixes failed prints", from "Kenneth from Obico" <support@obico.io>. This version needs a new sender name in SendGrid. The address and the reply address stay support@obico.io.

Both open on the same problem: a print failed, and now you have to work out why and what to change. Both are short plain text like batch 4, with the same video, download and announcement links. The download link is plain text, not a button, since the button didn't do better in batch 4.

**Version A**

> Hi [first name, or "there"],
>
> A print fails, and then comes the hard part: working out why, and which of a few hundred slicer settings to change. Most of us end up searching forums and trying one change per print.
>
> JusPrin 2 is an AI slicer built to take that part off your hands. Take a photo of the failed print and show it to JusPrin 2. It looks at your photo, your file and your settings, works out what went wrong, and changes the settings for you. You can also just tell it how you want a part printed, and it sets up the slice.
>
> Here's a short video of it: [video link]
>
> It's free if you bring your own AI: an API key from Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter, or an app you already use, like Claude Code or Codex. Or sign up in the app for 500 free credits, with no card needed. It runs on Windows, Mac and Linux.
>
> Download JusPrin 2: [GitHub latest release]
>
> Want the details and prices first? Read the announcement: [announcement link]
>
> If you have questions, just reply to this email.
>
> Kenneth Jiang
> Creator of Obico and JusPrin
>
> You're getting this because you have an Obico account.

**Version B** is the same from "Here's a short video" down. The first two paragraphs change:

> Obico tells you when a print goes wrong. Then you're left with the cleanup and the harder question: why did it fail, and what should you change so the next one doesn't?
>
> That question is why we built JusPrin, a free, open-source slicer from the Obico team with AI built in. Take a photo of the failed print and show it to JusPrin. It looks at your photo, your file and your settings, works out what went wrong, and changes the settings for you. You can also just tell it how you want a part printed, and it sets up the slice.

**How we'll pick a winner.** We'll compare opens, clicks and new JusPrin 2 sign-ups, matching each new account's email address to the group it came from. Opens show up within a day. Sign-ups will be few with 1,000 per group, so they'll likely show only a hint.

**After you approve:**
1. I add the "Kenneth from Obico" sender.
2. I upload the 2,000 people and build both campaigns.
3. I send test copies to k@obico.io.
4. You send both versions at the same minute.

The list is in `/Users/kenneth/.claude/jusprin2-email-data/batch5_candidates_2026-11-17.csv`.

Hi [%first_name | there%],

A print fails, and then comes the hard part: working out why, and which of a few hundred slicer settings to change. JusPrin 2 is a free AI slicer that does that part for you.

It's free because the slicer is open source and the AI is your own. Connect an API key from Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter, or an app you already use, like Claude Code or Codex. You pay that provider directly, and JusPrin charges you nothing. No AI account? Sign up in the app for 500 free credits, with no card needed.

Take a photo of the failed print and show it to JusPrin 2. It looks at your photo, your file and your settings, works out what went wrong, and changes the settings for you. You can also just tell it how you want a part printed, and it sets up the slice.

Here's a short video of it: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4NJm0vyzxA8

JusPrin 2 runs on Windows, Mac and Linux.

Download JusPrin 2: https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/releases/latest

Want the details and prices first? Read the announcement: https://www.obico.io/blog/introducing-jusprin-2/

If you have questions, just reply to this email.

Kenneth Jiang
Creator of Obico and JusPrin

You're getting this because you have an Obico account.
EOF

EOF

Hi [%first_name | there%],

A print fails, and then comes the hard part: working out why, and which of a few hundred slicer settings to change. JusPrin 2 is a free AI slicer that does that part for you.

It's free because the slicer is open source and the AI is your own. Connect an API key from Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter, or an app you already use, like Claude Code or Codex. You pay that provider directly, and JusPrin charges you nothing. No AI account? Sign up in the app for 500 free credits, with no card needed.

Take a photo of the failed print and show it to JusPrin 2. It looks at your photo, your file and your settings, works out what went wrong, and changes the settings for you. You can also just tell it how you want a part printed, and it sets up the slice.

Here's a short video of it: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4NJm0vyzxA8

JusPrin 2 runs on Windows, Mac and Linux.

Download JusPrin 2: https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/releases/latest

" Meet JusPrin 2, from the team behind Obico
A free AI slicer that works out why a print failed and fixes the settings. ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ 
Hi [%first_name | there%],

Obico tells you when a print goes wrong. Then you're left with the harder question: why did it fail, and what should you change so the next one doesn't? JusPrin 2, our free AI slicer, answers that for you.

It's free because the slicer is open source and the AI is your own. Connect an API key from Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter, or an app you already use, like Claude Code or Codex. You pay that provider directly, and JusPrin charges you nothing. No AI account? Sign up in the app for 500 free credits, with no card needed.

Take a photo of the failed print and show it to JusPrin 2. It looks at your photo, your file and your settings, works out what went wrong, and changes the settings for you. You can also just tell it how you want a part printed, and it sets up the slice.

Here's a short video of it: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4NJm0vyzxA8

JusPrin 2 runs on Windows, Mac and Linux.

Download JusPrin 2: https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/releases/latest

Want the details and prices first? Read the announcement: https://www.obico.io/blog/introducing-jusprin-2/

If you have questions, just reply to this email.

Kenneth Jiang
Creator of Obico and JusPrin

You're getting this because you have an Obico account.
[Sender_Name], [Sender_Address], [Sender_City], [Sender_State] [Sender_Zip]
Unsubscribe - Unsubscribe Preferences
"

# Global Claude Code Rules

## How to Communicate

Talk like a colleague explaining something out loud, not like a report.

1. **Full sentences, one idea each.** Lead with a concrete case (someone opens a file, chats twenty times, then runs out of credits) before any general point. Never pack a mechanism into a noun phrase like "hidden fair-use ceiling". Say what the person sees happen, step by step.

2. **No labels of your own.** Names you made up while working ("phase 2", "board 6a", "the M4 batch", "the three decisions") mean nothing to me. Name a thing by what it is or does. To ask about a screen, say where it is and send the picture.

3. **Ask decisions in full, as questions.** Start with "Decision needed". Give one paragraph per decision: what it is, why it's mine, the options with what each costs, and your pick. End it with a "?". Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or the report it's in. Don't hand me a choice you could settle yourself by searching or measuring.

4. **Mark proposals as proposals.** Keep apart what the code does today, what you propose, and what I have agreed to. Never write an idea I haven't approved as if it were settled. Before calling something "my rule", find my actual words.

5. **Report outcomes, not the journey.** Leave out problems you hit and solved unless they change what I do next. For an investigation, say what the problem was, how you solved it, what you tested and the result, and what's still open. Keep it under about 500 words.

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands
3. Only proceed after explicit user approval
4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

**Never commit or attempt to commit submodule updates.**

When `git status` shows modified submodules (e.g., `modified: some-submodule (new commits)`):
- Do not stage or commit the submodule change
- Do not include submodules when running `git add`
- Leave submodule management to the user

## Testing Principles

1. Always test your code change unless the change is not testable.

2. If the change is not testable, highlight the reason why it's not testable to get the user's attention.

3. By default, do end-to-end testing on everything that may potentially be impacted by your change on the local dev environment.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

5. Look for README files in the project for related info.

6. Check if the local dev is already running before you try to start it again.

## Software Engineering Principles

1. **Don't reinvent the wheel (avoid Not Invented Here).** Before building anything, check whether the codebase or the libraries it already uses do it, and reuse that. Re-implementing something is a decision that needs a stated justification.

## Where to Create Worktrees and Temporary Folders

This file is read by more than one coding tool, so each rule names the idea first and the tool-specific path second.

1. **Use the location your own tool already uses for worktrees.** Claude Code: `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`. Codex: `~/.codex/worktrees/`. If this session was started inside a worktree the tool created, put any further worktree beside it.
2. **Never create a worktree or a working folder in `~` or directly under `~/Projects`.** That includes sibling folders such as `<repo>-worktrees`. This holds for a different repo than the one the session started in: use that repo's tool-managed location (rule 1) or the scratch directory (rule 3).
3. **Short-lived worktrees, build output, logs, screenshots and scripts go in the session's scratch or temp directory** if the tool gives one (Claude Code names it in the session instructions). If it gives none, use a new folder under the system temp directory, not the home directory.
4. **Keep non-worktree files out of worktree folders.** Logs, screenshots and scripts do not belong beside the worktrees. They go in the scratch directory, or inside the one worktree they concern.
5. **Use absolute paths when creating a worktree.** A shell may reset its working directory between commands, and a path starting with `~` or `..` can land somewhere unintended.
6. **Say where it is.** After creating a worktree, tell the user its full path, and remove it and its branch when the work is finished and merged.

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.


## GCP / kubectl Credential Policy

Always use the service account `ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for all `gcloud` and `kubectl` operations. Before running any such command, switch to it:

```bash
gcloud config set account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

The personal account `k@obico.io` is reserved for the user's own interactive CLI use and its OAuth tokens expire — do not rely on it.

## Sentry Access

- Instance: `sentry.obico.io`
- API base: `https://sentry.obico.io/api/0/`
- Auth token: `REDACTED`
- Usage: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" <api_url>`

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Branches

- `jusprin-dev` is the development branch. Start each change on a new branch from it and land the change there. It began at `975c703f08`, the merge of OrcaSlicer 2.5.0, and contains the earlier development branches `jusprin-newui` and `ui-walkthrough`; start nothing new on those.
- `main` is the stable branch and GitHub's default branch: the repository's front page, its issue forms, and the workflows GitHub runs on a schedule come from it.
  - Never force-push `main`, so that people who cloned the repository never have to force-pull. Only in an extreme case with no other way out, and with Kenneth's yes, may an admin lift the GitHub protection that blocks force pushes and deletion.
  - For now `main` is also the release branch: it moves forward from `jusprin-dev` when a version is released, and releases are built from it. This may change if a separate release branch is added later.
- `jusprin-v1` holds JusPrin 1, for fixes to that version only.
- `jusprin-v2-poc` holds the experiments described below.
- Take each OrcaSlicer release into `jusprin-dev` as `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` rule 10 describes.

## Releasing

`.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml` builds a release into a draft on GitHub; its top comment says how to start it. It refuses the commit until it has all of these:

- The version, in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`, above every released JusPrin version.
- The release notes, in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md`.
- The Sentry secrets: `JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN`, the project the app sends error reports and crashes to, and `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG` and `SENTRY_PROJECT`, which upload each build's debug files and the pages' source maps. A platform's build fails unless Sentry then holds debug information with file and line for the app's own code (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh`) and a source map for each page as built (`sentry_page_maps.sh` beside it); the nightly build checks the same.
- The guide, `docs/guide/`, checked for that version. Run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai` on a built copy of the commit, fix every page it reports, and commit the pages with their pictures, skills and `docs/guide/checked-version.txt`, as `docs/guide/README.md` describes under "Before a release". That file names the version the check last passed for, not the commit. Ticking "Release without the guide check" on the workflow's Run workflow form skips this, and the draft's title then says so. A release started by pushing a `jusprin-release/` branch has no form, so it always needs the file.

## Error handling

Less is more. An error is **expected** only when the person can do something about it, such as sign in again, get more credits, update a key or check the network, and Kenneth decided what the product tells them. Every other error is **unexpected**: the person sees one generic sentence and a way to report the problem, and the report carries everything known, so that we can find the cause.

Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is something that user can do nothing about, just show the user a generic error message and give user a way to report a problem. On the back end though, we need to make sure we send as much info as possible to the Sentry server so that we can do root cause analysis. And that's it, nothing else." And: "When it comes to error handling, less is more."

The reporting function is `report_unexpected_error` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.hpp`). This repository has no expected-errors table yet.

### Expected errors

- Each has an entry in the expected-errors table: the cause, what the person sees, and what they can do next. A new entry needs Kenneth's yes; quote his words in the commit message.
- The test is what the person can do next. If the answer is "nothing" or only "try again later", the error is unexpected. An AI provider or our own server being slow, overloaded, down or limiting us is unexpected: the person can do nothing about any of them.
- Two causes that leave the person doing the same thing do not get separate sentences, codes or branches.
- A cause is "out of credits" or "no network". A status code, an exception type, or "the request was not valid" is not a cause.
- Each entry has a test, and each occurrence is counted.
- Handle them with normal control flow, not exceptions.

### Unexpected errors

- Write no code for them. Do not catch one, give it a default value, retry it, or give it a sentence of its own. Each of those is a guess about a failure nobody understands. It hides the failure and loses where it came from.
- Let the failure stop the work and travel up unchanged.
- A failure that arrives as a value, such as a status code, stops nothing by itself. Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop. Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it.
- One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure through the one reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side", with nothing more specific. No other code reports.
- A tool call that fails is shown as failed in the turn's activity line, its error goes to the AI model, and the turn goes on; no dialog opens. When the failure is the app's own and not the model's mistake, it is also reported, and only if the person has turned automatic reports on.
- When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected.
- The report carries as much as is known: the other side's status, request id and error text, and the request's own facts, such as the user, the chat, the turn and the model. The person is told none of it.
- Never record a failure as a success.
- A log line is not a report: it reaches nobody.

### Catching

- Catch an error only when it is an expected one and the code can recover from it, or at a boundary to translate it or add context, and then rethrow.
- Keep lower-level operations strict; the caller that owns the workflow enforces their preconditions.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering.

### Checks

- An agent reads the changed code against these rules and asks one question wherever the code decides what happened: can the person do something about it, and did Kenneth decide what they are told?
- Do not sort unexpected failures into kinds for the person, and do not bring Kenneth a question about the wording of a failure the person can do nothing about. On 2026-11-16 the code that kept five "try again" sentences apart was deleted for this reason.
- To audit a commit range, use the `error-handling` skill (`.claude/skills/error-handling/`). To check production for a period, use the `jusprin-production-check` skill in the tsd-enterprise repository.

## Build Commands

Build the Release configuration unless asked otherwise.

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config Release --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config Release --target all --

# Windows
cmake --build . --config Release --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/`; see [tests/AGENTS.md](tests/AGENTS.md) for where a new test belongs and the conventions to follow.

```bash
cd build && ctest -C Release --output-on-failure    # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r -C Release       # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print -C Release
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake); Moonraker and OctoPrint: `tests/printer_hosts/README.md` (Docker). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Documentation

- Docs live in `docs/`; the high-level design of a subsystem goes in `docs/HLSD/<subsystem>.md`.
- Describe the design as it stands — what the subsystem does, why it exists, and the constraints that shape it. Not the route that got there: no phases, task lists, status markers, or "before/after this PR" framing.
- Planning and investigation output (brainstorms, superpowers design and plan docs) stays in `docs/superpowers/`, which is gitignored. Never commit it.
- Write a doc only when the design is not evident from the code, and when a change invalidates an existing one, update it in the same PR.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Include what you use: include the header for every symbol a file uses, and keep headers compilable on their own. Never rely on the precompiled header or a transitive include. The `clang-tidy` CI job enforces this on changed lines; run the same check locally with `scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh` (`scripts\run_clang_tidy.ps1` on Windows), which sets up everything it needs
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.
- Wording the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca or OrcaSlicer: the model speaks as the app, and a second name reads as a second program. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards this too. Log lines may name Orca. A throw may only if it never reaches the model: tool results forward save and open errors as they are, and the guard does not see those strings.
- Always use `SetSizerAndFit(sizer)` instead of `SetSizer(sizer)` on top level window. Unless `SetSizer` must be called before the full layout is built, call `sizer->SetSizeHints(window)` afterwards in this case.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Before designing a screen or writing any on-screen text, follow `agent-docs/jusprin/design-guidelines.md`: whole-screen boards with real strings, the wording rule, and a cold-reader check on screenshots before and after building.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Pull requests

Before opening a pull request or posting on GitHub, read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), including its "If you are an AI agent" section.

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.
- For profile changes (`resources/profiles/<Vendor>/**`), check that `version` in the sibling `resources/profiles/<Vendor>.json` was bumped.
- For new or changed UI strings, check they follow [Writing translatable strings in the source](#writing-translatable-strings-in-the-source): no concatenated fragments, plural forms for counts, contexts for ambiguous words.
- For translation changes (`localization/i18n/**/*.po`), check that recurring terms match the [Localization glossary](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_glossary.md) for that language.

## Localization & translations

Catalogs live in `localization/i18n/<lang>/OrcaSlicer_<lang>.po`; the template is `OrcaSlicer.pot`.
See the [Localization guide](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_guide.md) for the human-facing version of these principles.

### Writing translatable strings in the source

Translators see one msgid at a time and cannot change the code around it, so each message must be complete in a single msgid. Use the wrapper that fits instead of assembling text from pieces:

- **One msgid per sentence, with placeholders.** Never build a message by concatenating translated fragments (`_L("A") + name + _L(" is B")`) or by splicing a translated word such as `_L("left")` into another sentence: the translator can't reorder or inflect the parts. Write `format(_L("%1% is too close to others"), name)`.
- **A count needs a plural form.** Don't write `file(s)` or leave a verb unchanged after a number. Use `_L_PLURAL("%1% object", "%1% objects", n)`. libslic3r has no plural lookup, so word the message so it doesn't depend on a count, or build it in the GUI.
- **An ambiguous word needs a context.** When a short string means different things in different places (verb or noun, a mode name, a CAD term), give each sense its own context with `_L_CONTEXT`/`_u8L_CONTEXT`/`L_CONTEXT`. Keep the most common sense without a context so its existing translations stay valid.
- **Mark every user-visible string** (`_L`/`_u8L`, or `L` where it is translated later) and list new source files in `localization/i18n/list.txt`: files that aren't listed are never extracted.
- Add a `// TRN` comment above a new string whose meaning or placeholders aren't obvious.
- Never choose behavior by comparing translated text; compare ids or flags.

See `.claude/skills/orca-translations/references/source-audit.md` for the full checklist.

### Terminology

- Use the [Localization glossary](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_glossary.md) as the source of truth for recurring terms, so the same English term is always rendered the same way within a language, and terms that must stay in English (brand/product names, acronyms, materials, file formats, G-code tokens, macros/variables/identifiers) are not translated.
- If a term's established translation changes, update both the affected `.po` files and the glossary (`developer_reference/glossary/<lang>.tsv` in the wiki, then regenerate) so they stay in sync.
- Translate the *meaning*, not the words. Check what the string actually controls before translating it — English reuses one word for different things. `Flow ratio` (multiplier), `Flow Rate` (throughput) and `Flow Dynamics` (pressure compensation) are three different terms; `extruder` may mean the toolhead, the feeder motor, or the nozzle depending on the string.
- Reuse one template per recurring message shape (`Failed to connect to …`, `Are you sure you want to …?`), even where the English wording varies.

### Editing rules

- Only edit `msgstr` — **never** change `msgid`, and never "fix" wrong English in the translation alone. Report the source string instead.
- Preserve exactly: placeholders (`%s`, `%d`, `%1%`, `%zu`, `%%`), every `\n` (count *and* position, including leading/trailing), leading/trailing spaces, HTML tags, `℃`, and the file's encoding and line endings.
- **Never reorder positional arguments** in a `c-format` string. If the msgid is `%d` then `%s`, that order must hold — swapping them breaks at runtime.
- `msgctxt` separates homonyms — always read it. `Back`/`Camera View` is the rear view of the 3D navigator, while `Back`/`Navigation` is the go-back button; `Top` exists in the *Alignment*, *Layers* and *Camera View* senses.
- When a string needs disambiguating, add context in the source (`_L_CONTEXT`/`_u8L_CONTEXT`), don't work around it in the translation.
- A literal `%` inside a string xgettext flagged `possible-c-format` will fail `msgfmt`. Fix it with a `// xgettext:no-c-format, no-boost-format` comment above the string in the source — do not mangle the translation or use `%%` in text that is never passed through printf.
- Plural entries: read `nplurals` from the catalog's `Plural-Forms` header (it is **not** always 2 — ja/ko/zh/th/vi use 1, ru/cs/pl/lt use 3, uk uses 4). Each form must be genuinely inflected for its quantity; repeating one sentence across all forms is a bug in Slavic/Baltic languages, though it is correct for Turkish and Hungarian.
- An entry whose `msgstr` equals its `msgid` is untranslated even though it is not empty; a plural entry with any empty form is likewise incomplete.
- Mark machine-produced translations with an `# AI Translated` translator comment. Don't add it to a human translation you didn't actually rewrite.
- When you can't be sure of a machine translation's meaning or UI wording, also add `# Needs human review: <what to check>`. Never use `fuzzy` for this — fuzzy entries are hidden from users.
- Don't reflow or re-wrap unrelated entries — keep the diff limited to the strings you changed.

### Verifying

- `scripts/run_gettext.bat --full` (Windows) regenerates the template, merges every catalog and compiles the `.mo` files. It must exit 0.
- Or check a single catalog with `msgfmt --check-format --check-header -o <out>.mo localization/i18n/<lang>/OrcaSlicer_<lang>.po`. Without `--check-header`, msgfmt skips the placeholder check in plural forms.
- Fuzzy entries are not shown to users. If you correct one, clear its `fuzzy` flag, otherwise the fix never ships.
