tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. The cache is positional: agent() calls replay from cache up to the first call that failed, no longer matches the earlier run (edited, added, removed or reordered) or never started in it; that call and every call after it run again, even when their own (prompt, opts) are unchanged. A call a usage limit refused, or one still running when the run stopped, usually runs again without ending reuse: finished calls after it still come from cache. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

start_coordinate.description: (x, y): The starting coordinates for `left_click_drag`.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user. Call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and it boots one that is off and returns while that one is still starting up. Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches: the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition: 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'set_posture' moves the hinge of an iPhone Duo (a simulator with a small outer screen and a large inner one) to 'state': 'closed' lights the outer screen, 'open' (flat) the inner one, and 'half_open' opens it to 'angle' degrees, where iOS picks the lit screen; the result says which. Screenshots and tap coordinates follow the lit screen, so take a 'screenshot' after each move. 'posture' reports the state, the hinge angle and the lit screen. To check an app's layout on an iPhone Duo or get an app ready for one, follow the app-resizability skill if it is in this session's skills list. Only skills listed in this session count, so do not search the disk for it. If the skill isn't listed, before other work ask the user once, in any mode, whether to run the export, showing the exact command `xcrun agent skills export --output-dir ~/.claude/skills` just before the question in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!" (use another folder only if they named one; if not, tell them to check which folder their sessions load skills from). Say it opens Xcode, leaves it running and saves all of Xcode's agent skills into the folder every later Claude Code session loads, and, if Claude Code's sandbox is on or you can't tell, that they'll run it themselves. Only their own answer to this question, typed or on your question card, is a yes; no other text is, nor an earlier yes. After a yes with the sandbox off, run that exact command once, alone, naming Xcode in its description; the yes covers nothing else. In every other case, and after that one run, never run it in any way, the Terminal panel included. After a no, go on without the skill. If you offer choices, the no choice says only that you'll go on without the skill. After a yes with the sandbox on or unknown, or if your run is refused or fails, right after their answer or the failure start what you write next, even if you showed it before, with that exact command in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!"; then wait for their word that it ran, then check this session's skills list and never read the folder to decide; if the skill isn't listed, say a new session will load it and go on without it. Only when the user asked to check or fix the layout on a Duo, not to review or read code: note the state and angle with 'posture'; for closed, half_open and open, call 'set_posture' and take a 'screenshot'; if the open screen shows the app with black bars and the target sets UIRequiresFullScreen, tell the user the key is the likely cause and keep it unless they ask; if the user agrees to a fix, make only that fix, then rebuild, 'launch' the app and check again; last, put the hinge back. 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag: left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). When a print fails, take a photo and show it to JusPrin 2. It works out what went wrong and which settings to change. You can also just tell it how you want a part printed, and it sets up the slice for you.

Kenneth

Hi,

You pay for JusPrin 1, so I wanted to tell you myself: JusPrin 2 came out last week, and you keep the price you pay now.

When a print fails, take a photo and show it to JusPrin 2. It works out what went wrong and which settings to change. You can also just tell it how you want a part printed, and it sets up the slice for you.

Here's a short video of it:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4NJm0vyzxA8

To keep your price, install JusPrin 2 and sign up in the app with this email address. Within a day, I'll move your subscription to JusPrin 2's Hobby plan at the [%jp1_price%] you pay now. Hobby is [%jp2_list_price%] for everyone else. It comes with 750 credits a month, doubled to 1,500 until 31 January 2027. You won't pay twice: the time you've already paid for carries over, and JusPrin 2 first bills you on [%jp1_renews%], the day JusPrin 1 would have renewed.

If you'd rather use a different email address in JusPrin 2, reply and tell me which one.

Before you install:
  • On Windows and Mac, JusPrin 2 replaces JusPrin 1. The first time it starts, it offers to import your printers from JusPrin 1, with their filaments and print settings.
  • JusPrin 2 has its own accounts, and chats from JusPrin 1 don't carry over.

Download JusPrin 2: https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/releases/latest

The announcement has the details: https://www.obico.io/blog/introducing-jusprin-2/

Thanks for supporting JusPrin from the start.

Kenneth

content.text:
I've added a paragraph to the email to paying JusPrin 1 subscribers. It says JusPrin 2 is far better than JusPrin 1 and asks them to try it and see for themselves. The change is only in my local copies so far. SendGrid has signed you out, so the campaign itself still has the old text, and nothing has been sent.

The new paragraph comes right after the opening:

> Hi,
>
> You pay for JusPrin 1, so I wanted to tell you myself: JusPrin 2 came out last week, and you keep the price you pay now.
>
> **JusPrin 2 is far better than JusPrin 1. I'd rather you see that for yourself than take my word for it, so please install it and try it on your next print.**
>
> When a print fails, take a photo and show it to JusPrin 2. …

I didn't write "infinitely better" because it reads as hype. "Far better", followed by an invitation to see for themselves, makes the same claim in a way readers will believe. Tell me if you want stronger wording.

Once you're signed in, I'll put the new text into the campaign and send the test copy to k@obico.io to check it. I'll still ask before sending the real campaign. Whether to add the line telling subscribers to add a card before their renewal date is also still your call.

Please sign in to SendGrid in the Chrome tab I opened (it's on the login page now), and say "signed in" when you're done.

    """Creates the lots nobody buys: the first month's, once per account, and
    after it the free credits of an account without a subscription, a new lot

    on the unique source_ref. A yearly plan's lot for the month under way comes

def ensure_lots(user_id: int, now: datetime = None) -> None:
    """Creates the lots nobody buys: the first month's, once per account, and
    after it the free credits of an account without a subscription, a new lot

        'credits_remaining': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_SIGNUP_CREDITS,
        'expires_at': now + relativedelta(months=1),
    })
    if now < signup.expires_at or _is_subscribed(user_id):

        'credits_remaining': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_FREE_CREDITS,

const H=" JusPrin 2 is out, and you keep your JusPrin 1 price
JusPrin 2 is out, and you keep the price you pay for JusPrin 1. ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ ͏ 
Hi,

You pay for JusPrin 1, so I wanted to tell you myself: JusPrin 2 came out last week, and you keep the price you pay now.

JusPrin 2 is far better than JusPrin 1. I'd rather you see that for yourself than take my word for it, so please install it and try it on your next print.

When a print fails, take a photo and show it to JusPrin 2. It works out what went wrong and which settings to change. You can also just tell it how you want a part printed, and it sets up the slice for you.

Here's a short video of it:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4NJm0vyzxA8

To keep your price, install JusPrin 2 and sign up in the app with this email address. Like every new account, you get 500 free credits to use in your first month. Within a day, I'll move your subscription to JusPrin 2's Hobby plan at the [%jp1_price%] you pay now. Hobby is [%jp2_list_price%] for everyone else. It comes with 750 credits a month, doubled to 1,500 until 31 January 2027. You won't pay twice: the time you've already paid for carries over, and JusPrin 2 first bills you on [%jp1_renews%], the day JusPrin 1 would have renewed.

If you'd rather use a different email address in JusPrin 2, reply and tell me which one.

Before you install:
  • On Windows and Mac, JusPrin 2 replaces JusPrin 1. The first time it starts, it offers to import your printers from JusPrin 1, with their filaments and print settings.
  • JusPrin 2 has its own accounts, and chats from JusPrin 1 don't carry over.

Download JusPrin 2: https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/releases/latest

The announcement has the details: https://www.obico.io/blog/introducing-jusprin-2/

Thanks for supporting JusPrin from the start.

Kenneth

You're getting this because you subscribe to JusPrin 1.

Hi,

You pay for JusPrin 1, so I wanted to tell you myself: JusPrin 2 came out last week, and you keep the price you pay now.

JusPrin 2 is far better than JusPrin 1. I'd rather you see that for yourself than take my word for it, so please install it and try it on your next print.

When a print fails, take a photo and show it to JusPrin 2. It works out what went wrong and which settings to change. You can also just tell it how you want a part printed, and it sets up the slice for you.

Here's a short video of it:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4NJm0vyzxA8

To keep your price, install JusPrin 2 and sign up in the app with this email address. Like every new account, you get 500 free credits to use in your first month. Within a day, I'll move your subscription to JusPrin 2's Hobby plan at the [%jp1_price%] you pay now. Hobby is [%jp2_list_price%] for everyone else. It comes with 750 credits a month, doubled to 1,500 until 31 January 2027. You won't pay twice: the time you've already paid for carries over, and JusPrin 2 first bills you on [%jp1_renews%], the day JusPrin 1 would have renewed.

If you'd rather use a different email address in JusPrin 2, reply and tell me which one.

Before you install:
  • On Windows and Mac, JusPrin 2 replaces JusPrin 1. The first time it starts, it offers to import your printers from JusPrin 1, with their filaments and print settings.
  • JusPrin 2 has its own accounts, and chats from JusPrin 1 don't carry over.

Download JusPrin 2: https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/releases/latest

The announcement has the details: https://www.obico.io/blog/introducing-jusprin-2/

Thanks for supporting JusPrin from the start.

Kenneth

#!/bin/zsh
S=/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/c2adecd8-a1fc-4e82-9512-79ed47bbae43/scratchpad
for i in {1..12}; do
  /opt/homebrew/bin/gog gmail search 'subject:"keep your JusPrin 1 price" newer_than:1h "500 free credits"' --account k@obico.io --json --no-input --max 1 > $S/t.json
  id=$(python3 -I -c 'import json,sys;d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]));d=d if isinstance(d,list) else (d.get("threads") or d.get("messages") or []);print(d[0]["id"] if d else "")' $S/t.json)
  [ -n "$id" ] && break; sleep 15
done
echo "id=$id"; [ -z "$id" ] && exit 1
/opt/homebrew/bin/gog gmail thread get $id --account k@obico.io --json --no-input > $S/t.json
python3 -I - $S/t.json <<'PY'
import json,base64,sys

pl=msgs[-1].get('payload',msgs[-1])
def parts(p):
    yield p
    for c in p.get('parts',[]) or []: yield from parts(c)
for p in parts(pl):
    if p.get('mimeType')=='text/plain' and p.get('body',{}).get('data'):
        t=base64.urlsafe_b64decode(p['body']['data']+'==').decode('utf-8','replace').replace('\r\n','\n'); print(t[:900])
PY
rm -f $S/t.json
EOF
chmod +x $S/check_test.sh

That's why I wrote "to use in your first month" instead of implying the credits last forever.

The local copies of the email in `~/.claude/jusprin2-email-data/` match what's in SendGrid.

<cross-session-message from="local_c2b9f42b-4cb3-4805-978b-8b715d50a555" from-name="Build the JusPrin 1 loyalty Hobby plan with one-time codes">
Answers on the JusPrin 1 loyalty-code plan, point by point. Each point says whether it is built, agreed by Kenneth, or only proposed. The code is tsd-enterprise commit 65dd4972f0. It runs on staging (image obi.4140) and is not on production.

Where Kenneth's own words exist, I quote them. Where I only have the plan as your session's task gave it to me (prices, 750 credits, the coupon end date, ending the old subscription at end of term), I say that: it came from the task, and I haven't seen Kenneth's own words for it.

1. How a subscriber gets the code
- Built: the code goes in this email, one per person, through a single new SendGrid custom field, `jp1_code`.
- The draft that uses the field: /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_120b7ae4-455f-4969-ab29-1246e7b02a33/jusprin1-loyalty-email-draft.html
- A code is a one-time Chargebee coupon code. On the test site they look like JP1-FWSX-BXTH. The live codes don't exist yet.
- A code is not tied to an email address or an account. Any signed-in JusPrin 2 account that has no plan can use it once.
- The $41.99 subscriber's code comes from a separate batch of codes. That batch is what makes the page show $41.99.

2. Where they enter it
- Built and agreed by Kenneth: "Go with this option. Also, currently the billing page is served from the server anyway, right? If this is the case, why do we need an app update in order to do it? the coupon code is being asked on the chargebee checkout page, right?"
- The path in the app:
  1. Click the gear, then "Get more credits". This opens the Credits and plans sheet.
  2. Under the plan cards: "Got a code in our email to existing subscribers? Enter your code".
  3. A page titled "Keep the price you pay now" opens, with a "Code" field and a "Continue" button.
  4. Two cards appear. Their buttons say "Subscribe to Hobby yearly" and "Subscribe to Hobby monthly".
  5. Chargebee's checkout opens with the code already applied.
- No app update is needed.
- The page does not work in a plain browser on jusprinv2.obico.io. Opened there, it says "Sign in to use your code. Open Credits and plans from JusPrin, signed in to your JusPrin account."
- None of these pages says "JusPrin 1". Kenneth: "Existing JustPrint subscribers have never heard of the term JustPrint One. phrases in a way that they can understand." He approved the wording from screenshots.

3. Plans and prices
- Built; the prices come from the task.
- Everyone sees Hobby yearly at $59.99 a year and Hobby monthly at $6.99 a month.
- The $41.99 subscriber's code shows Hobby yearly at $41.99 a year and the same $6.99 monthly.
- These prices never appear on the regular Credits and plans page.

4. What checkout charges, and when
- Built.
- The code takes 100% off the first period. They pay $0.00 at checkout.
- The free period is a fixed full year or month from the day they check out. It is not tied to their JusPrin 1 renewal date.
- The first real charge comes one period after checkout. On the staging checkout, made on 25 Nov 2026, it read "Next charge on November 25, 2027 $59.99".
- After that they pay the loyalty price for as long as they keep the plan. The page says: "You pay for Hobby what you pay now, for as long as you keep it."

5. Their JusPrin 1 subscription
- Built only as a helper; ending the subscriptions is a manual step.
- Nothing cancels it automatically. The command `jusprin1_pending_moves` lists every live JusPrin 1 subscription whose email address now has a JusPrin 2 plan, with its renewal date.
- Someone has to run that command daily and end each listed subscription on Obico's Chargebee site at the end of its term, never immediately, because ending it now refunds the unused part. This comes from the task. Who runs it has not been decided.
- Risk of paying both: a JusPrin 1 subscription that reaches its renewal date before anyone ends it renews and charges them again, and that charge would need a manual refund. Otherwise they don't pay both, because JusPrin 2's first period is free.

6. Credits
- Built.
- The loyalty plans grant 750 credits a month, the same as regular Hobby. That number comes from the task.
- The launch double applies: the staging page shows "1,500 credits a month until 31 Jan, then 750." The offer ends at midnight Pacific on 1 Feb 2027.
- Every new JusPrin 2 account gets 500 sign-up credits (`JUSPRIN_V2_SIGNUP_CREDITS`). A new test account started with 500.
- I haven't checked whether sign-up credits expire.

7. Deadline
- Built; the date comes from the task.
- The coupon ends 28 Feb 2027.
- The "Enter your code" line disappears from Credits and plans on 1 Mar 2027.
- A used, expired or archived code gets: "That code has been used or has expired. Reply to the email…"

8. Production status
- Staging only.
- Kenneth: "go ahead. to stg only. don't go live to prod before I approve"
- Before the email can go out, each of these needs Kenneth's go-ahead:
  1. Move production to image obi.4140.
  2. On the live Chargebee site `jusprinv2`, create the two loyalty items and three prices, a new 100%-off coupon, and the two batches of codes. The coupon must be named "Existing subscribers: first period free", with invoice name "Existing subscriber: first period free", because checkout shows that name next to the code.
  3. Fill `jp1_code` per subscriber in SendGrid.
  4. Put the email into draft campaign 22659147.
  5. Send it.
- Separately, a live coupon `jusprin1-move-first-term` has a guessable id and gives anyone a free first Hobby period. Archiving it closes that.
- Full details are in jusprin1-loyalty-handover.md in the same notes folder.

JusPrin 2 is out, and you keep the price you pay for JusPrin 1. Your code is inside.

Hi,

You pay for JusPrin 1, so I wanted to tell you myself: JusPrin 2 came out last week, and you keep the price you pay now.

JusPrin 2 is far better than JusPrin 1. I'd rather you see that for yourself than take my word for it, so please install it and try it on your next print.

When a print fails, take a photo and show it to JusPrin 2. It works out what went wrong and which settings to change. You can also just tell it how you want a part printed, and it sets up the slice for you.

Here's a short video of it:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4NJm0vyzxA8

Your code:

[%jp1_code%]

It gets you JusPrin 2's Hobby plan at the [%jp1_price%] you pay now, yearly or monthly, and makes your first year (or first month, if you pick monthly) free, so you pay nothing today. Hobby is [%jp2_list_price%] for everyone else. It comes with 750 credits a month, doubled to 1,500 until 31 January 2027.

To use it:

- Install JusPrin 2 (link below) and sign in or sign up. Using this email address makes it easiest for me to match you up.
- Click the gear at the top right, then Get more credits, then Enter your code at the bottom of the page.
- Type the code above and pick yearly or monthly.

The code works once, until 28 February 2027. Checkout still asks for a card or PayPal, for when the plan renews.

You won't pay twice. Once you've signed up, I'll stop your JusPrin 1 subscription from renewing on [%jp1_renews%]. You keep JusPrin 1 until then, and nothing more is charged or refunded for it.

If you use JusPrin 2 with a different email address, reply and tell me which one, so I know whose JusPrin 1 to stop. If you've already bought a JusPrin 2 plan, reply too, and I'll sort it out.

Before you install:

- On Windows and Mac, JusPrin 2 replaces JusPrin 1. The first time it starts, it offers to import your printers from JusPrin 1, with their filaments and print settings.
- JusPrin 2 has its own accounts, and chats from JusPrin 1 don't carry over.

Download JusPrin 2: https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/releases/latest

The announcement has the details: https://www.obico.io/blog/introducing-jusprin-2/

Thanks for supporting JusPrin from the start.

Kenneth

You're getting this because you subscribe to JusPrin 1.
Kenneth from JusPrin, 651 N Broad St, Suite 206, Middletown, DE 19709

The plan has changed in a way that means rewriting most of the email. I no longer move anyone by hand. Each subscriber gets a one-time code in the email. In JusPrin 2 they click the gear, then "Get more credits", then "Enter your code", and check out for Hobby at their old price, with the first year (or first month) free. This works on staging and isn't on production yet.

**What the email has to change:**

1. **The "To keep your price" paragraph gets replaced.** It currently says "Within a day, I'll move your subscription" and "JusPrin 2 first bills you on [their JusPrin 1 renewal date]". Both are now wrong. The new paragraph gives their code and the three steps to use it. It also says the first year or month is free, so they pay nothing today, and that the code works once, until 28 February 2027. Their first charge comes one full period after checkout, not on their JusPrin 1 renewal date. The loyalty session's draft already has this text.
2. **The line about adding a card goes away.** Chargebee's checkout asks for a card or PayPal, so there's nothing left for you to decide there.
3. **"You won't pay twice" now depends on you.** It now reads: "Once you've signed up, I'll stop your JusPrin 1 subscription from renewing on [date]." Someone has to run the `jusprin1_pending_moves` command every day and end each listed subscription at the end of its term. Nobody has been assigned to that yet. If it slips, a subscriber's JusPrin 1 renews and charges them, and that charge needs a manual refund. The first monthly renewals are 7 and 10 December.
4. **A new SendGrid field.** The new field holds each person's code, so the email can't go out until the live codes exist. The subscriber who pays $41.99 gets their code from a separate batch.
5. **The name "JusPrin 1".** You said existing subscribers have never heard the name "JusPrin 1", and the app's code pages already avoid it. The email uses it in the subject, the opening, the "far better" line, the install notes and the footer. I propose the same treatment here, for example "the JusPrin you use now". The subject would become "JusPrin 2 is out, and you keep the price you pay now".

Here's the draft for the code plan. It doesn't use the name "JusPrin 1", following what you said about existing subscribers never having heard it. Text in [brackets] is filled in per person from SendGrid.

---

**Subject:** JusPrin 2 is out, and you keep the price you pay now

**Preview line:** Your code to keep your price is inside.

Hi,

You subscribe to JusPrin, so I wanted to tell you myself: JusPrin 2 came out last week, and you can keep the price you pay now.

When a print fails, take a photo and show it to JusPrin 2. It works out what went wrong and which settings to change. You can also just tell it how you want a part printed, and it sets up the slice for you.

Here's a short video of it:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4NJm0vyzxA8

Once you've used JusPrin 2 for a few prints, I don't think you'll want to go back. But that's your call to make.

Your code: **[code]**

It gets you JusPrin 2's Hobby plan at the [$59.99 a year] you pay now, for as long as you keep it. Hobby is [$100 a year] for everyone else. Your first year is free (your first month, if you pick monthly), so you pay nothing today. Hobby comes with 750 credits a month, doubled to 1,500 until 31 January 2027. Like every new account, you also get 500 free credits for your first month.

To use it:
- Install JusPrin 2 and sign up in it. Use this email address if you can, so I can match you up.
- Click the gear, then Get more credits, then Enter your code at the bottom.
- Type your code and pick yearly or monthly. Checkout asks for a card or PayPal, which is charged only when the free year or month ends.

The code works once, until 28 February 2027.

You won't pay twice. Once you've used your code, I'll stop your current JusPrin subscription from renewing on [21 September 2027]. You keep it until then, and nothing more is charged or refunded for it.

If you sign up for JusPrin 2 with a different email address, reply and tell me which one, so I know which subscription to stop. If you've already bought a JusPrin 2 plan, reply too, and I'll sort it out.

Before you install:
- On Windows and Mac, JusPrin 2 replaces the JusPrin you have now. The first time it starts, it offers to import your printers, with their filaments and print settings.
- JusPrin 2 has its own accounts, and your old chats don't carry over.

Download JusPrin 2: https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/releases/latest

The announcement has the details: https://www.obico.io/blog/introducing-jusprin-2/

Thanks for supporting JusPrin from the start.

Kenneth

*Footer:* You're getting this because you subscribe to JusPrin.

---

**For the subscriber who cancelled,** the "You won't pay twice" paragraph is replaced with: "Your current subscription already ends on [8 August 2027], so nothing more is charged for it."

**Things to check as you review:**

- **The "go back" line.** It now says "go back" without naming the old app, which avoids "JusPrin 1" and reads less like a sales pitch. It sits after the video, so readers see what JusPrin 2 does before the claim.
- **Picking yearly or monthly.** The price sentence names only what each person pays now. The code page shows both options (for example $59.99 a year or $6.99 a month), so a monthly subscriber can pick yearly there. The email doesn't spell this out, to keep it short.
- **Where the gear is.** I haven't seen the gear in the main window myself. The loyalty session's screenshots show "Get more credits" in Preferences › Account. I'll check the gear's location in the app before this goes into SendGrid.
- **The 500 credits.** They expire a month after sign-up. The app's Account page shows "Sign-up credits … Expires 25 Dec" for a test account made on 25 November.

content.text:
Here's the redraft. I made your four changes, cut the details that made it sound like we were hiding something, and checked the steps for using the code against the app. Text in [brackets] is filled in per person.

---

**Subject:** JusPrin 2 is out, and you keep your price

Hi,

JusPrin 2 is out.

When a print fails, take a photo and show it to JusPrin 2. It works out what went wrong and which settings to change. You can also just tell it how you want a part printed, and it sets up the slice for you. Once you've used JusPrin 2, you won't want to go back.

Here's a short video of it:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4NJm0vyzxA8

As a thank-you for subscribing, the code below moves your subscription to JusPrin 2 at the [$59.99 a year] you pay now, for as long as you keep it. Everyone else pays [$100 a year]. Your first year on JusPrin 2 is free (your first month, if you choose monthly), and like every new account, you start with 500 free credits.

Your code: **[code]**

To use it:
- Install JusPrin 2 and sign up with this email address.
- Click the gear at the top right of the Home screen. Under Account, click Get more credits, then Enter your code.
- Enter your code and check out.

The code works until 28 February 2027. Once you've moved, your current subscription won't renew, so you never pay for both.

If you'd rather use a different email address, or you've already bought a JusPrin 2 plan, just reply to this email.

Before you install:
- On Windows and Mac, JusPrin 2 replaces the JusPrin you have now. The first time it starts, it offers to import your printers, with their filaments and print settings.
- JusPrin 2 has its own accounts, and your old chats don't carry over.

Download JusPrin 2: https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/releases/latest

The announcement has the details: https://www.obico.io/blog/introducing-jusprin-2/

Thanks for supporting JusPrin from the start.

Kenneth

*Footer:* You're getting this because you subscribe to JusPrin.

---

**What I cut:**
- The line about telling them myself, and "last week".
- "That's your call to make".
- The Hobby credit numbers (750 a month, doubled to 1,500 until 31 January).
- How we stop the old subscription, and their renewal date.
- That checkout asks for a card or PayPal (the checkout page asks for it anyway).
- That a code works only once.

**For the subscriber who already cancelled,** I'd drop "Once you've moved, your current subscription won't renew, so you never pay for both." Theirs already won't renew.

**The steps for using the code come from the app's own text.** On the Home screen, the gear at the top right opens Preferences, and Preferences › Account has "Get more credits". I took that from the app's source and the loyalty session's screenshots. I haven't clicked through it myself.

**2. What happens to my money.** My best reading is that I pay nothing for the first year and then $59.99 a year after that. - "Your first year on JusPrin 2 is free (your first month, if you choose monthly)". I read it twice. It made me ask what monthly costs.
- "Under Account, click Get more credits, then Enter your code." It's an odd path, and it ties my subscription to credits again.
- "Once you've moved, your current subscription won't renew". It doesn't say what happens to the time I've already paid for.
- "Thanks for supporting JusPrin from the start." I joined a year ago, so this feels like a form letter.

**5. What's missing.**
- What credits are, what 500 of them buys, and what happens when they run out.
- Whether the subscription includes AI use.
- The monthly price.

content.text:
The cold reader got the gist on one skim: JusPrin 2 is out, the code keeps their price, and the first year is free. It said the offer felt mostly like a favour. Three things made it hesitate, and one of them made it suspicious.

**What the cold reader tripped on:**

1. **"You start with 500 free credits" made it suspicious.** It didn't know what credits are, and it wondered whether its subscription still covers the AI. In its words, it "reads like pay-per-use is coming."
2. **It couldn't tell what it would pay, or when.** It read "the $59.99 a year you pay now" next to "first year is free" twice. It also guessed that "check out" means entering a card today, and the email doesn't say so. The words "if you choose monthly" made it ask what monthly costs.
3. **It didn't know what happens to the time it has already paid for.** It read "won't renew" and wondered whether it loses those months, or whether it has to cancel the old plan itself.
4. **Smaller points:**
   - "Once you've used JusPrin 2, you won't want to go back" read as salesy. Next to "replaces the JusPrin you have now", it sounded like it *couldn't* go back.
   - "Get more credits" seemed an odd place to enter a subscription code.
   - "Thanks for supporting JusPrin from the start" felt like a form letter to someone who joined a year ago.

**Proposed revision (only the changed parts; the rest stays as before):**

> As a thank-you for subscribing, the code below moves your subscription to JusPrin 2. Your first [year] is free. After that, you pay the [$59.99 a year] you pay now, for as long as you keep it, instead of the [$100 a year] everyone else pays. Checkout asks for a card, but nothing is charged until your free [year] ends.
>
> Your plan includes credits for the AI: 1,500 a month until 31 January, then 750, plus 500 extra to start. A message to the AI uses 1 credit, or 5 with the Expert model.

> To use it:
> - Install JusPrin 2 and sign up with this email address.
> - Click the gear at the top right of the Home screen, then Get more credits. At the bottom of that page, click Enter your code.
> - Enter your code and check out.
>
> The code works until 28 February 2027. Your current subscription runs to the end of the time you've already paid for, then stops, so you never pay for both.

> Thanks for supporting JusPrin.

**What each change does:**

- **The first-period sentence names only each person's own period.** Yearly subscribers read "year" and monthly subscribers read "month", so nobody wonders about the other price. That needs one more SendGrid field.
- **The money paragraph now answers what, when, and whether a card is charged now.** It still doesn't explain how anything works behind the scenes.
- **The credits sentence says the subscription covers the AI.** That was the cold reader's real worry. The 1 and 5 credits per message come from the app's own Credits and plans page, and the 1,500-then-750 figures come from the loyalty plan on staging.
- **"Runs to the end of the time you've already paid for, then stops"** says what happens without saying how we do it.

**I kept "Once you've used JusPrin 2, you won't want to go back."** You asked for that line. The cold reader's only problem with it was that it sits next to "replaces". If that bothers you, the install bullet could add "Your printers and settings come with you."

## figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

FILE SESSION:
Once the target fileKey is known, call create_session with that key and a concise task description before search_design_system, get_libraries, use_figma, or any other file tool. This applies to read-only tasks too. If a new file is needed, call create_new_file first, then create_session with the returned file key. Reuse the returned UUID as the sessionId argument on eligible file tools for subsequent work on that task, including calls to other files.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_figma flows; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use-figjam/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-diagram — MANDATORY before calling generate_diagram; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md
- /figma-design-to-code — MANDATORY before calling get_design_context; fallback: skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md

Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:

- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → FigJam file, use get_figjam
- figma.com/slides/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → Figma Slides file
- figma.com/spec/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → Figma Specs file, load the figma-spec skill and use use_figma

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW (Figma → code):
MANDATORY: load the /figma-design-to-code skill BEFORE calling get_design_context — it carries the full workflow (adapting the reference, reusing existing project components and tokens, and honoring the response's hints by priority). content.text:
Yes, public Hobby gets the same credits. In the server's plan table (`tsd-enterprise/web_ent/settings_ent.py`), public Hobby, monthly and yearly, gets 750 credits a month, the same as the loyalty Hobby plans. Until the launch offer ends at midnight Pacific on 1 February 2027, every plan's monthly credits are doubled, so Hobby gets 1,500.

The 1,000 and 500 you're remembering are other things:

- **1,000 a month is Workshop**, the $20-a-month plan (2,000 during the launch offer).
- **500 is the one-time credit pack** for $10 (1,000 during the launch offer). New accounts also get 500 sign-up credits, which expire a month after sign-up.

The app's Credits and plans page shows the same numbers: Hobby "750 → 1,500 credits a month", Workshop "1,000 → 2,000", and the credit pack "500 → 1,000".

So "1,500 a month until 31 January, then 750, plus 500 extra to start" is right for the subscribers' Hobby plan.

input.description: Check Workshop's standard-message rule

content.text:
Yes. Workshop, monthly or yearly, makes Standard messages free, so they're unlimited. Its 1,000 credits a month (2,000 during the launch offer) are spent only on Expert messages, at 5 credits each.

Here's where that comes from in tsd-enterprise:

- **The setting.** Both Workshop plans carry `unlimited_basic: True` in `web_ent/settings_ent.py`.
- **The charge.** `web_ent/jusprin/ledger/ledger.py:100` charges nothing for a Standard message on a plan with that setting.
- **The wording.** The Credits and plans page shows "Standard messages cost 0 credits." on the Workshop card (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/web.py:233`).

Hobby doesn't have that setting, and neither do the loyalty Hobby plans for JusPrin 1 subscribers. On them, a Standard message costs 1 credit, so the subscriber email's "A message to the AI uses 1 credit, or 5 with the Expert model" is right.
